settings.definition_quote: In each round, the decision maker selects an arm from a finite set $\cX$. Each arm $x\in\cX$ has an unknown parameter $\theta(x)\in \mathbb{R}$, and when this arm is chosen in round $t$, the decision maker observes a real-valued random variable $Y(x,t)$ with expectation $\theta(x)$ and distribution $\nu(\theta(x))$. ... The parameter $\theta$ lies in a compact set $\Theta$ that encodes the structural properties of the problem. (Bernoulli observations) $\theta(x) \in [0,1]$ and $\nu(\theta(x)) =$Ber$(\theta(x))$

source.label: th:low
source.quote: Let $\pi\in \Pi$ be a uniformly good algorithm. For any $\theta\in \Theta$, we have: \lim\inf_{T\to\infty} \frac{R^\pi(T,\theta)}{\ln~T} \ge C(\theta), where $C(\theta)$ is the value of the optimization problem ...

results.notes: Theorem holds for general observation distributions nu; recorded under Bernoulli setting (and separately Gaussian). Derived by applying Graves & Lai (1997).

source.label: th:optimal
source.quote: If Assumptions~\ref{ass:unique}, \ref{as:div_continuous}, \ref{as:mu_continuous} and \ref{ass:unique_sol} hold and either Assumption~\ref{ass:bernoulli} or \ref{ass:gaussian} holds, then under the algorithm $\pi=$OSSB($\varepsilon,\gamma$) with $\varepsilon < {1 \over |\cX|}$ we have: \lim\sup_{T\to\infty} {R^\pi(T) \over \ln~T} \le C(\theta) F(\varepsilon,\gamma,\theta)

results.notes: Computational complexity depends on structure; not polynomial in general. Proof gives F = (1+2 eps psi/C)(1+gamma).

source.label: th:optimal
source.quote: If Assumptions ... hold and either Assumption~\ref{ass:bernoulli} or \ref{ass:gaussian} holds, then under the algorithm $\pi=$OSSB($\varepsilon,\gamma$) with $\varepsilon < {1 \over |\cX|}$ we have: \lim\sup_{T\to\infty} {R^\pi(T) \over \ln~T} \le C(\theta) F(\varepsilon,\gamma,\theta)

symbols.G: G(gamma,|X|), finite constant from KL concentration lemma
symbols.delta_kappa: delta(kappa)>0 continuity radius such that C(lambda)<=(1+kappa)C(theta) etc.

source.quote: Putting everything together we obtain the finite-time regret upper bound: R^{\pi}(T) \le \mu^\star(\theta) \left( G(\gamma,|\cX|) + {2 |\cX| \over \varepsilon \delta^2(\kappa)}\right) + (C(\theta)(1 + \kappa) + 2 \varepsilon \psi(\theta) ) (1+\gamma) \ln~T.

results.notes: Not a numbered theorem; stated in text and appendix proof. The proof uses ln T in thresholds, so horizon treated as known-ish; algorithm itself uses ln t, uncertain. Applies to Gaussian case too.
